h: Standing on the banking and other highlights
p: Seeing the remains of the steep banked track is something special. It's hard to believe how fast drivers were going on that bumpy concrete over a century ago, often in cars that looked little more than an engine with a seat bolted on. Head up the Test Hill too, built to see how cars coped with a sharp climb, and you'll get a real sense of the daredevil spirit of the place.

The aviation story is just as gripping. Brooklands was where many famous British aircraft were built, including the Wellington bomber, and the aircraft collection reflects that heritage. Look out for the Wellington recovered from Loch Ness after years underwater, a remarkable survivor and a real talking point.
A few tips for your day:

Wear comfy shoes, as the site is spread out and you'll do a fair bit of walking between hangars and halls. Keep an eye on the event calendar, because motoring and aviation days often bring extra cars and displays out. If you're visiting with younger children, plan in a few breaks, as there's a lot to take in and it's easy to wear little legs out.

Petrolheads, aviation fans, families with curious kids and anyone with an interest in British engineering will all find plenty to love. Even people who claim they aren't interested in cars often come away surprised by how much they enjoyed the stories.

Weybridge itself is a pleasant Surrey town by the Thames and the River Wey, so a riverside walk is a nice way to wind down afterwards. Painshill, the landscaped 18th-century garden at nearby Cobham, is also close enough to combine on a longer trip.
